title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc.; Order Disapproving a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To List and Trade Shares of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF Under BZX Rule 14.11(e)(4), Commodity-Based Trust Shares
summary: On 6 April 2022, the Federal Register published an SEC order (Release No. 34-94571) disapproving Cboe BZX Exchange's proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 1, to list and trade shares of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF under BZX Rule 14.11(e)(4), the exchange's Commodity-Based Trust Shares listing standard, File No. SR-CboeBZX-2021-051. The trust's sponsor is 21Shares US LLC. The order, dated 31 March 2022, concludes BZX had not met its burden under Exchange Act Section 6(b)(5) to show its rules were designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts: the Commission found BZX had not established a comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreement with a regulated market of significant size in bitcoin, and that Amendment No. 1's added statistical analysis did not resolve the Commission's earlier concerns.
why_it_matters: This order shows the legal test the SEC applied to early spot-bitcoin exchange-traded product listings: an exchange had to show either a surveillance-sharing agreement with a market of significant size in the underlying asset or other adequate anti-fraud safeguards, and general statistical arguments about bitcoin market behavior were not enough on their own. Naming the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF here reflects only what the SEC's own order states about that specific, historical proposal.

citations.quote: designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices and to protect investors
